Subject: Request: technical safeguards evidence for cross-border exports (RFP-45872)

Hi Naomi,

As part of Aurelia Health's procurement for patient-facing AI routing, our security and privacy team has asked for detailed evidence about cross-border data exports and technical safeguards associated with your hosted and private deployment options. This is focused on EU patient data moving to US and regional processing variants.

Concretely, we need:
- A per-feature matrix listing where tokenized content or model inputs/outputs may leave the EU (hosting, logging, backups).
- Evidence of legal/technical controls used for EU->US transfers (e.g., SCCs/DPA annex, encryption-in-transit and at-rest, key ownership options).
- Details on routing policies, fallbacks, and processor/subprocessor lists for Dedicated and Private modes.
- Audit log retention and access controls (how long, who, and how to obtain logs for audits).
- Example network topology for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment and the steps to ensure no egress without approval.

Can you provide an initial package by EOD Tuesday (2026-11-23)? We will likely follow with a few clarifying technical questions.

Thanks,
Sarah Brennan
Sr. Security Analyst | Aurelia Health

Naomi / team — draft package attached. Summary below and inline answers to Aurelia's bullets. Attachment: redwood_export_safeguards_matrix.xlsx (tabbed: Overview, PerFeatureExport, LegalControls, NetworkVPC, AuditLogs)

Executive summary (2 lines): Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private modes. By default, hosted API endpoints in EU regions keep model inference in region; however, customer-configured fallbacks and routing policies can route to US model variants. Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) ensures no egress to Redwood unless explicitly enabled.

Inline answers (high level):
1) Per-feature export matrix: see tab PerFeatureExport. Highlights: Hosted generation (text/chat) in EU region -> stays in-region unless a routing policy triggers a fallback (note: fallbacks are governed by per-tenant routing rules and logged). Embeddings: by default generated in-region; however, vector-store backups sent to cloud backups depending on customer config. Logs & backups: request logs (redacted tokens) are stored per-region but may be aggregated for analytics in the US if customer enables cross-region analytics.

2) Legal/technical controls for EU->US transfers:
- DPA Annex (SCCs equivalent): included as draft (see dpa_annex_draft_for_aurelia.pdf).
- Encryption: TLS1.2+ (recommended TLS1.3) in transit; AES-256-GCM at rest.
- KMS: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KEK via KMS/HSM) for Dedicated and Private; hosted accounts default to Redwood-managed keys with optional customer-managed keys for Enterprise tiers.

3) Routing policies & subprocessors:
- Smart routing policy definitions (latency, cost, region) are tenant-configurable. Fallbacks are explicit rules; we include an opt-out for cross-region fallback in the DPA annex.
- Subprocessors list: see NetworkVPC tab for infra partners (GCP EU regions, S3-compatible backups in region, optional US analytics ingest via partner DataLens). Full subprocessors list is in our public registry (link in doc).

4) Audit logs: retention default 90 days for request traces; 1 year for security audit logs. We provide log export in newline-delimited JSON; access via Console or an S3 export (signed URL). For Private deployments, logs can be retained on-prem.

5) Network topology: attached network_topology_v1.png shows VPN peering, private endpoints, and optional egress blockers. For Private/VPC we publish a runbook to cut all outbound egress at time of deployment until customer enables specific routes.

Notes for sending to Aurelia: we should include a short cover letter clarifying that the hosted default behavior keeps inference in-region unless explicitly configured otherwise, and call out which checklist items require contract-level commitments (DPA annex language).

Marissa
Product Security Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_export_safeguards_matrix.xlsx, dpa_annex_draft_for_aurelia.pdf, network_topology_v1.png

Hi Sarah — thank you for the clear ask. Attached is a technical package for Aurelia's review: redwood_export_safeguards_matrix.xlsx (per-feature mapping and notes), dpa_annex_draft_for_aurelia.pdf (contract language we suggest for exports/fallbacks), and network_topology_v1.png (private deployment topology).

Short answers up front:
- By default, regional-hosted inference remains in-region. Cross-region routing only occurs when customers enable fallback policies or when they explicitly route to a US model variant. We have an opt-out clause in the DPA annex to prohibit region fallback for regulated accounts.
- For Dedicated and Private: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and on-prem storage for audit logs.
- Audit logs: security/audit logs are retained for 1 year; request traces are 90 days by default. We can provide SOC 2 Type II report access via secure link and a redacted sample of audit events under NDA.

Next steps: please confirm if a call on Tue 11/24 at 10:30AM CET works to walk through the matrix and DPA language. If there are targeted questions beforehand, send them and we'll prioritize.
